## 1. This week's analysis


# Download VCF 

```{r}
dir.create("data/week06", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create("output/week06", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

base <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/course-fish546-2026/Roberts-546/main"
download.file(paste0(base, "/output/04-stacks-demo/populations/populations.snps.vcf"),
              "data/week06/eelgrass-demo.vcf")
download.file(paste0(base, "/data/stacks-demo/popmap.tsv"),
              "data/week06/popmap.tsv")
```

# Read header

```{r}
lines  <- readLines("data/week06/eelgrass-demo.vcf")
header <- lines[startsWith(lines, "##")] # Lines starting with ## describe the file: the program that made it, and what each INFO and FORMAT field means.
header
```


# Read variant table

```{r}
vcf <- read.delim("data/week06/eelgrass-demo.vcf", comment.char = "",
                  skip = length(header), check.names = FALSE)
names(vcf)[1] <- "CHROM"   # was "#CHROM"
dim(vcf)                   # 213 SNPs; 9 fixed columns + 20 samples
vcf[1:3, 1:10]

samples <- names(vcf)[10:ncol(vcf)]
popmap  <- read.delim("data/week06/popmap.tsv", header = FALSE, col.names = c("sample", "pop"))
stopifnot(all(popmap$sample == samples))
```



# Pull our genotypes and depth

```{r}
gt <- sapply(vcf[, samples], function(x) sub(":.*", "", x))
# Missing genotypes ("./.") have no depth, so they become NA
dp <- suppressWarnings(sapply(vcf[, samples],
                              function(x) as.numeric(sub("^[^:]*:([^:]*):.*", "\\1", x))))
rownames(gt) <- rownames(dp) <- vcf$ID
table(gt)

# Count ALT alleles per genotype: 0, 1, or 2
alt <- apply(gt, 2, function(g) c("0/0" = 0, "0/1" = 1, "1/1" = 2)[g])
rownames(alt) <- vcf$ID

colSums(is.na(alt))   # missing genotypes per sample
```


# Summerize each SNP

```{r}
snps <- data.frame(
  id         = vcf$ID,
  locus      = vcf$CHROM,
  pos        = vcf$POS,
  n_called   = rowSums(!is.na(alt)),
  mean_depth = rowMeans(dp, na.rm = TRUE),
  alt_freq   = rowSums(alt, na.rm = TRUE) / (2 * rowSums(!is.na(alt)))
)
snps$maf <- pmin(snps$alt_freq, 1 - snps$alt_freq)   # minor allele frequency
summary(snps)
hist(snps$maf, breaks = 20, main = "Minor allele frequency", xlab = "MAF")
```


# Filter and count before and after


```{r}
keep <- snps$n_called >= 18 & snps$maf >= 0.05
nrow(snps)   # before
sum(keep)    # after
table(called_18 = snps$n_called >= 18, maf_05 = snps$maf >= 0.15)
```

# Compare two sites

```{r}
filtered <- snps[keep, ]
is_pb <- popmap$pop == "PB"
af <- function(a) rowSums(a, na.rm = TRUE) / (2 * rowSums(!is.na(a)))

filtered$freq_PB   <- af(alt[keep, is_pb])
filtered$freq_SJ   <- af(alt[keep, !is_pb])
filtered$freq_diff <- abs(filtered$freq_PB - filtered$freq_SJ)
filtered <- filtered[order(-filtered$freq_diff), ]
head(filtered, 10)

plot(filtered$freq_PB, filtered$freq_SJ, xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, 1),
     xlab = "ALT allele frequency, PB", ylab = "ALT allele frequency, SJ",
     pch = 19, col = ifelse(filtered$freq_diff > 0.5, "red", "grey40"))
abline(0, 1, lty = 2)   # SNPs on this line have the same frequency at both sites

write.csv(filtered, "output/week06/snp-summary-filtered.csv", row.names = FALSE)
sum(filtered$freq_diff > 0.5)
```




# What to write

1. What the INFO and FORMAT fields in this VCF contain. This file has no QUAL score (.). What does that mean for filtering?

> The info field in a VCF contains metadata describing the variants while the formant field in a VCF contains the genotype, read depth, genotye quality and allelic depth. If the file has no quality score then that means they have no read depth and are removed from the sample.  

2. Your before and after counts, and why the MAF filter removed nothing here.

> Before filtering I had 213 counts and after filtering I had 194 counts. The minor allele frequency filter did not remove any counts becuase the minimum MAF was 0.05 which means when we filtered for anything 0.05 and above all counts met that threshold. 

3. Change one threshold (for example n_called >= 20, or maf >= 0.2) and report how the counts and the number of strongly different SNPs change.

> I changed the MAF threshold to 1.5 and 6 counts were removed from the analysis and there were 27 strongly different SNPs.   

4. A caveats paragraph. With 10 plants per site, how much would you trust a single SNP’s frequency difference? What would you need before calling a SNP a sign of local adaptation?

> 10 sites does not a provide a lot of information and if there is only one SNP at a location that is not strong evidence to indicate a difference, especially if some reads are filetered out during the different steps. You would need multiple SNPs across a large amount of samples to have confidence of local adaptation.  




## 2. Reflection questions

1. What does a variant call represent?

> A variant call represents a file that stores gene sequence variations and identifies changes in sequenced genome compared to the reference genome. 

2. How can read depth, genotype quality, or filtering thresholds change a biological interpretation?

> These three things can change a biological interpretation because depending on where you put the threshold for filtering or how good the reads are you could be losing data that is important for the confidence in identification or inversly you could be allowing bad reads to be in the data giving false confidence in species identification.  

3. What is your strongest current project output, and what is the riskiest step remaining?

> The strongest output I currently have for my project is a bar graph with percent of species at each site. The riskiest step remaining is turning that infomration into a diversity index for each site.
